newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: IMF to base Guatemala standby plan on peace accord.
newsitem.headline: IMF to base Guatemala standby plan on peace accord.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will use economic targets outlined in Guatemala's recent peace accords as part of a new stand-by agreement, IMF director Michel Camdessus said on Monday.
"This is an historic event and the IMF has also taken an historic decision," Camdessus told a news conference.

"In these accords Guatemalans themselves outlined goals of raising taxes to 12 percent of GDP and sustained GDP growth of 6.0 percent a year until 1999...Those goals will be used by the IMF to sign a new agreement with Guatemala," he said, speaking on the last day of a four-day visit to Guatemala.
Leftist rebels and the government signed a peace treaty ending 36 years of civil war last December 29. The accords included general agreements on social and economic goals.
Camdessus said an agreement with Guatemala could not be reached until Guatemala's Congress approved laws to allow the economic goals in the accords to be reached.
Guatemala obtained pledges of some $1.9 billion in aid from donor countries in order to carry out the peace accords' promises, but the money is conditional upon a stand-by agreement with the IMF.
"It is important to increase the percentage of taxes to GDP, which barely reaches 7.0 percent here. Many more poor countries than Guatemala have a better percentage than that," Camdessus said.
"I think the country is on the right track, but it needs the consensus of all sectors of society. This is a moment during which the country can either take off or sink," he added.
